## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D game where the player controls a barefoot giantess walking through a miniature city and crushing vehicles and buildings.

## Requirements
- Deliver the playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser-based Three.js game with keyboard and touch controls, a 90-second timer, impact scoring, and stomp effects.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added responsive game UI, 3D miniature city, stylized barefoot character, movement, stomping, destruction/scoring, timer, replay, and optional sound.
- Confirmed JavaScript syntax with `node --check --input-type=module < game.js`.
- Ran the game in Playwright, started it, tested Space and ArrowUp input, and captured/inspected `screenshots/latest.jpg`.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. If further verification is needed, inspect gameplay behavior and mobile layout; changes are currently uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Responsive UI styling and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, city models, character, controls, stomp logic, scoring, and rendering.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent visual check.

## Important Context
- Playwright reported a 404 for `/favicon.ico`; it did not prevent the game from loading.
- The city and giantess are procedurally assembled from Three.js primitives; Three.js is imported from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`.

Implemented the playable browser game in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`. It includes a procedural miniature city, a barefoot giantess, keyboard and touch movement, stomping and destruction, scoring, a 90-second timer, and replay.

I verified the JavaScript syntax and tested starting the game and pressing Space in Playwright. The latest visual check is `screenshots/latest.jpg`. I assumed a browser-based Three.js game with procedural art; the changes are uncommitted.
